=Describe this image in a single continuous paragraph of plain prose — no bullet points, numbered lists, markdown, or headers, and no introductory phrases like "This image shows" or "The image depicts". Open directly with the subject matter.

Treat this as an OCR-plus-context task: transcribe every piece of visible text exactly as written (titles, axis/column labels, category names, numeric values, units, source or attribution lines, watermarks), preserving Indonesian number formatting (e.g. "." as thousands separator) rather than reformatting or rounding. Where a label is paired with a value (a category next to a bar, a row in a table), keep that pairing intact and state them together, and preserve the order and grouping shown in the image (e.g. left column before right column, top to bottom) rather than mixing them up. If the image contains many similar rows (a long list of regions or categories with values), transcribe all of them once each, in order — do not summarize a long list down to a few examples, but also never repeat an item or a block of items you've already stated. If incidental UI chrome is visible (a browser button, a "Close" button, a cursor, a watermark unrelated to the content) mention it only in passing if at all, and don't let it interrupt the flow of the actual content.

After transcribing the text, briefly state in your own words what the image is illustrating or comparing, so the paragraph conveys both what is written and what it means. Write in full sentences, and make sure your final sentence is complete — do not trail off or cut the description short partway through a thought or list.

If a caption is provided below, use it only to clarify who/what is shown (e.g. resolve ambiguity) — do not quote or repeat it, and do not let it override what's actually visible in the image.

Caption from sender: {{ $('Telegram Trigger').item.json.message.caption ? $('Telegram Trigger').item.json.message.caption : 'None' }}

options.systemMessage: You are a chat summarization bot for a team's Telegram channel. Analyze the conversation history provided and produce a clear, concise summary of key points, following these rules: 1. Filter out noise — ignore greetings, small talk, single-word replies, bot chatter, and unclear or pointless chatter (e.g. random mentions of body parts/genitals with no real topic or substance). 2. Focus on substance — highlight the main topics discussed, decisions made, problems identified, and action items. 3. Exclude crude, vulgar, or explicit sexual talk (dirty jokes, sexual banter, etc.). However, DO include discussions that are genuinely about sexual/reproductive health, medical topics, or education — do not filter those out just because they mention sex. 4. Attribute key ideas or decisions to the person who raised them, when clear from the chat. 5. Write the summary in Indonesian (Bahasa Indonesia). 6. Output must use Telegram-compatible HTML tags only (e.g. bold, italic) — never Markdown or asterisks. Wrap any English words, loanwords, or technical terms in italic tags. 7. Match the summary length to the time range or number of chat being covered: up to 3 hours or last 100 chats → max 1000 characters; up to 6 hours or last 200 chats → max 2000 characters. Stay strictly within the limit so it fits in a single Telegram message. If the chat history is not already provided in the user message, use the Supabase tool to retrieve it before summarizing.

parameters.query:
WITH RECURSIVE
vector_seed AS (
  SELECT id, content, metadata, created_at,
         row_number() OVER (ORDER BY similarity DESC) AS rnk
  FROM match_documents_v2(
    '[{{ $json.embedding.values.join(",") }}]'::vector,
    40,
    YOUR_GROUP_CHAT_ID
  )
),
keyword_seed AS (
  SELECT id, content, metadata, created_at,
         row_number() OVER (ORDER BY ts_rank(content_tsv, query) DESC) AS rnk
  FROM public.telegram_knowledge, to_tsquery('simple', '{{ $json.keywordPattern }}') query
  WHERE chat_id = YOUR_GROUP_CHAT_ID
    AND '{{ $json.keywordPattern }}' <> ''
    AND content_tsv @@ query
  ORDER BY ts_rank(content_tsv, query) DESC
  LIMIT 40
),
fused AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(v.id, k.id) AS id,
    COALESCE(v.content, k.content) AS content,
    COALESCE(v.metadata, k.metadata) AS metadata,
    COALESCE(v.created_at, k.created_at) AS created_at,
    (1.0 / (60 + COALESCE(v.rnk, 1000))) + (1.0 / (60 + COALESCE(k.rnk, 1000))) AS hybrid_score
  FROM vector_seed v
  FULL OUTER JOIN keyword_seed k ON v.id = k.id
),
all_seed AS (
  (SELECT id, content, metadata, created_at, hybrid_score
   FROM fused ORDER BY hybrid_score DESC LIMIT 15)

  UNION

  (SELECT f.id, f.content, f.metadata, f.created_at, f.hybrid_score
   FROM vector_seed v JOIN fused f ON v.id = f.id
   WHERE v.rnk <= 10)

  UNION

  (SELECT f.id, f.content, f.metadata, f.created_at, f.hybrid_score
   FROM keyword_seed k JOIN fused f ON k.id = f.id
   WHERE k.rnk <= 10)
),
ancestors AS (
  SELECT tk.id, tk.content, tk.metadata, tk.created_at, tk.message_id, tk.reply_to_message_id, tk.chat_id, 0 AS depth, s.hybrid_score
  FROM public.telegram_knowledge tk JOIN all_seed s ON tk.id = s.id
  UNION ALL
  SELECT parent.id, parent.content, parent.metadata, parent.created_at, parent.message_id, parent.reply_to_message_id, parent.chat_id, a.depth + 1, a.hybrid_score
  FROM public.telegram_knowledge parent
  JOIN ancestors a ON parent.message_id = a.reply_to_message_id AND parent.chat_id = a.chat_id
  WHERE a.depth < 10
),
descendants AS (
  SELECT tk.id, tk.content, tk.metadata, tk.created_at, tk.message_id, tk.reply_to_message_id, tk.chat_id, 0 AS depth, s.hybrid_score
  FROM public.telegram_knowledge tk JOIN all_seed s ON tk.id = s.id
  UNION ALL
  SELECT child.id, child.content, child.metadata, child.created_at, child.message_id, child.reply_to_message_id, child.chat_id, d.depth + 1, d.hybrid_score
  FROM public.telegram_knowledge child
  JOIN descendants d ON child.reply_to_message_id = d.message_id AND child.chat_id = d.chat_id
  WHERE d.depth < 10
),
combined AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (id) id, content, metadata, created_at, hybrid_score
  FROM (
    SELECT id, content, metadata, created_at, hybrid_score FROM ancestors
    UNION ALL
    SELECT id, content, metadata, created_at, hybrid_score FROM descendants
  ) u
  ORDER BY id, hybrid_score DESC NULLS LAST
)
SELECT id, content, metadata, created_at, hybrid_score
FROM combined
ORDER BY hybrid_score DESC NULLS LAST, created_at;

parameters.text:
Extract all readable text from this PDF document, preserving structure and reading order.

First output this header block:
Title: [document title, or "Untitled" if none is visible]
Document Type: [journal article / research paper / report / news article / invoice / form / presentation / other]
Language: [primary language(s) detected]

Then extract the full body text:
- Preserve original reading order, headings, and section breaks.
- Transcribe body text exactly as it appears. Do not paraphrase, summarize, or invent content.
- For any table, chart, or diagram, insert a brief plain-language explanation of what it shows, placed inline at the point where it appears (not moved elsewhere), wrapped as [Table/Figure: explanation]. This is the one place paraphrasing is allowed.
- If any part is illegible or unclear, mark it as [illegible] rather than guessing.

Return ONLY the header block and the extracted text. Do not add conversational filler, summaries, or intro/outro text.

options.systemMessage:
=You are an intelligent Telegram Chat Assistant. CRITICAL LANGUAGE RULE: Detect the language of the User's Question (English or Bahasa Indonesia only — never any other language). Your ENTIRE reply must be written in that same language, from greeting to closing line, regardless of what language the retrieved context snippets are written in. Do not mix languages in one answer. Examples: - Question: "shortcut to go to the next sheet in excel" → respond entirely in English. - Question: "cara pindah ke sheet berikutnya di excel" → respond entirely in Bahasa Indonesia. Your job is to answer group chat inquiries based ONLY on the provided context retrieved from a vector database. ### TASK 1. Identify the core user question/inquiry (from the context, or from the query if passed separately). 2. Read through the retrieved chat history / document snippets to summarize or directly answer the question. 3. If specific details (e.g., pricing, reviews, explicit answers) are missing, synthesize what IS known (e.g., who sells it, open PO status, discussions) and state clearly what remains unanswered. 4. Output the response in clean HTML suitable for Telegram's HTML parse mode. 5. Before writing your final answer, confirm to yourself which language the User's Question is in, then write only in that language — do not let the language of the retrieved context influence your choice. ### OUTPUT RULES — TELEGRAM HTML ONLY - Telegram's HTML parser supports ONLY these tags: , , , , 
. NO OTHER TAGS ARE ALLOWED, INCLUDING 
    , 
  • , 
      , 
      , 
      , 
      , 
      -
      , , . Using any of these will make the message fail to send.
- For lists, do NOT use 
        /
      • . Instead, write each item on its own line starting with '• ' (a bullet character), separated by newline characters.
- Cite each source individually — never combine multiple numbers into one bracket (write [1] [2] [4], not [1, 2, 4]).
- When you use information from a numbered source in the context, cite it immediately after the relevant sentence using its bracket number, e.g. [1]. Only cite numbers that were actually given to you in the context — never invent one that wasn't provided.

parameters.text:
=You are screening an image shared in a job/gig-work Telegram group to classify what kind of payment-related image it is, if any.

Message caption/text from the poster, if any (use ONLY to help identify a paying company or payment method not visible in the image itself — never invent one): "{{ $('Telegram Trigger').item.json.message.caption ?? '' }}"

=== ONLY DIRECT PROOF COUNTS ===
Direct proof is any of:
(a) a screenshot of an actual payment/banking app or wallet showing the transaction itself,
(b) an email or in-app receipt showing transaction details,
(c) a payout/earnings notification sent DIRECTLY BY the platform or employer to the recipient — e.g. "Your payout of $X is on its way", a payslip-style email, an app notification stating an amount and status. This still counts as direct proof even if the same email/message ALSO contains unrelated marketing, referral-program, or cross-sell content (e.g. "Earn more through referrals", an "Explore" button) elsewhere in the message — ignore that marketing portion and extract only from the actual payout notice,
(d) a bot-generated notification card from THIS group's own bot (headers like "INVOICE / BILL" or "VERIFIED PAYMENT").

If the image is instead a screenshot of a social media post, chat message, or forum thread that merely TALKS ABOUT or DISPLAYS a payment as part of a longer post — recognizable by social-platform UI chrome such as: an avatar + username + "Follow"/role-badge header, like/comment/share/bookmark counts, a post-age label ("8h", "22h", "2d"), a "Translate" option, "View activity", or nested reply/comment threads — this is a REPOST/TESTIMONIAL, not direct proof, even if it contains a visible amount, a "successful"/"completed" status, or persuasive claims about earnings. Set Category to "not_payment" in this case, regardless of what payment-looking content is embedded inside it.

=== PRODUCT / COURSE LISTINGS ARE NOT PAYMENTS ===
An ad or storefront-style listing for a course, ebook, service, or product (price/currency badge next to a product title or thumbnail, "buy now"-style layout, with NO transaction status and NO invoice framing directed at a specific buyer) is NOT a payment screenshot — set Category to "not_payment" even though a price/currency amount is visible.

Set Category to exactly one of:
- "paid": a completed payout/transfer, shown as DIRECT proof (see above) — status wording like "Completed", "Successful", "Sent", "Submitted", "Penarikan sukses" all count.
- "pending": a payout/payment shown as DIRECT proof that is scheduled, processing, in transit, or awaiting approval — not yet completed/arrived. Includes payout notification emails saying funds are "on its way" or "should appear within X business days".
- "bill_invoice": an invoice, bill, or payment request shown as DIRECT proof — money owed, not money received. Includes course/product purchase cards explicitly framed as an invoice/bill.
- "not_payment": the image isn't direct payment/financial proof — including product/course/service ads, storefront listings, and social-media/chat reposts or testimonials that merely display or discuss a payment.
- "other": something payment-related that doesn't fit the above.

Regardless of Category, extract whatever of the following is visible — don't leave fields empty just because Category isn't "paid":
- Paying_Company: the employer, client, or company the money is coming FROM (or billed BY, for invoices), if named. Empty string if not shown.
- Amount: the amount AND currency combined into one string, currency placed where it naturally belongs (e.g. "USDC 99.34", "$1,XXX.XX", "USD X53.47"). If digits are blurred/covered/blacked-out/scribbled, replace each hidden digit with X following normal digit grouping — a hidden group after a thousands comma is exactly 3 X's (e.g. "$1,XXX", never "$1,X"), a hidden cents group after a decimal point is exactly 2 X's (e.g. "$1,XXX.XX"). If the whole amount is hidden, write "redacted". Empty string only if no amount appears anywhere.
- Date: a date/time that is part of the PAYMENT CONTENT itself — e.g. "sent on...", an issue date, a due date, a transaction timestamp inside the message or receipt body. Do NOT use timestamps from surrounding UI chrome that aren't part of the payment content — an email/inbox app's "received at" time, the phone's status bar clock, a notification badge time, a social post's "Xh" age label, etc. If the payment content itself doesn't state a date, leave this empty — don't substitute a nearby UI timestamp. The date format should look like 1 January 2026.
- Payment_Method: whatever best identifies how/where the money moved or is billed through — a processor/app/bank name (Airtm, PayPal, Deel, Wise, a bank name) OR a generic method (Bank Transfer, Wire, Crypto) if no named service is shown. Use whichever is actually visible; don't guess a name that isn't there. If nothing is visible in the image, check the caption text above before leaving this empty.

Respond with ONLY a single valid JSON object, no markdown, no code fences, no commentary, matching exactly:
{
  "Category": string,
  "Paying_Company": string,
  "Amount": string,
  "Date": string,
  "Payment_Method": string
}

parameters.query:
WITH day_messages_raw AS (
  SELECT id, created_at, content, metadata
  FROM public.telegram_knowledge
  WHERE (metadata->>'created_at_gmt7')::timestamp >= (date_trunc('day', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Jakarta') - INTERVAL '1 day')
    AND (metadata->>'created_at_gmt7')::timestamp <  date_trunc('day', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Jakarta')
    AND metadata->>'chat_id' = 'YOUR_GROUP_CHAT_ID'   -- <-- filter to the target chat/group
),
day_messages AS (
  -- collapse multi-chunk blob rows (same source message, split into pieces by the
  -- text splitter) into ONE row per message, keeping the earliest chunk as representative
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (COALESCE(metadata->>'message_id', id::text))
    id, created_at, content, metadata
  FROM day_messages_raw
  ORDER BY
    COALESCE(metadata->>'message_id', id::text),
    COALESCE((metadata->'loc'->'lines'->>'from')::int, 0) ASC,
    created_at ASC
),
thread_names(thread_id, thread_name) AS (
  VALUES
    (SCAMMER_THREAD_ID, 'Scammer'), (CROWDGEN_THREAD_ID, 'Crowdgen'), (MERCOR_THREAD_ID, 'Mercor'),
    (JOB_OPENING_THREAD_ID, 'Job Opening'), (ONGOING_PROJECT_THREAD_ID, 'Ongoing Project'), (TELUS_THREAD_ID, 'Telus'),
    (INCOGNITO_THREAD_ID, 'Incognito'), (RWS_THREAD_ID, 'RWS'), (WELO_THREAD_ID, 'Welo'),
    (ONEFORMA_THREAD_ID, 'OneForma'), (VERIFIED_PAYOUT_THREAD_ID, 'Verified Payout'), (IMERIT_THREAD_ID, 'iMerit'),
    (PROLIFIC_THREAD_ID, 'Prolific'), (PAIR_RECORDING_THREAD_ID, 'Pair Recording Indo'), (INVISIBLE_THREAD_ID, 'Invisible'),
    (CODING_CLASS_THREAD_ID, 'Coding Class'), (ENGLISH_CLASS_THREAD_ID, 'English Class'), (DATAANNOTATION_THREAD_ID, 'DataAnnotation'),
    (TMAXXX_THREAD_ID, 'TMaxxx'), (OUTLIER_THREAD_ID, 'Outlier'), (TIPS_TRICKS_THREAD_ID, 'Tips & Tricks'), (BABEL_AUDIO_THREAD_ID, 'Babel Audio')
),
thread_counts AS (
  SELECT metadata->>'thread_id' AS thread_id, COUNT(*) AS message_count
  FROM day_messages
  WHERE metadata->>'thread_id' IS NOT NULL AND metadata->>'thread_id' <> ''
  GROUP BY metadata->>'thread_id'
),
top_threads AS (
  SELECT tc.thread_id,
         COALESCE(tn.thread_name, tc.thread_id) AS thread_name,
         tc.message_count
  FROM thread_counts tc
  LEFT JOIN thread_names tn ON tn.thread_id = tc.thread_id::bigint
  ORDER BY tc.message_count DESC
  LIMIT 3
),
top_members AS (
  SELECT split_part(COALESCE(metadata->>'sender_name', metadata->>'username'), ' ', 1) AS first_name,
         COUNT(*) AS message_count
  FROM day_messages
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY message_count DESC
  LIMIT 3
)
SELECT
  (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(dm.metadata->>'sender_name', dm.metadata->>'username'))
    FROM day_messages dm
  ) AS active_members,
  (
    SELECT string_agg(
      format('%s: %s',
        COALESCE(dm.metadata->>'sender_name', dm.metadata->>'username', 'unknown'),
        dm.content
      ),
      E'\n' ORDER BY (dm.metadata->>'created_at_gmt7')::timestamp
    )
    FROM day_messages dm
  ) AS messages,
  (SELECT json_agg(row_to_json(top_threads)) FROM top_threads) AS top_threads,
  (SELECT json_agg(row_to_json(top_members)) FROM top_members) AS top_members;

WITH week_messages_raw AS (
  SELECT id, created_at, content, metadata
  FROM public.telegram_knowledge
  WHERE (metadata->>'created_at_gmt7')::timestamp >= date_trunc('week', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Jakarta')
    AND (metadata->>'created_at_gmt7')::timestamp <  date_trunc('week', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Jakarta') + INTERVAL '7 days'
    AND metadata->>'chat_id' = 'YOUR_GROUP_CHAT_ID'   -- <-- filter to the target chat/group
),
week_messages AS (
  -- collapse multi-chunk blob rows (same source message, split into pieces by the
  -- text splitter) into ONE row per message, keeping the earliest chunk as representative
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (COALESCE(metadata->>'message_id', id::text))
    id, created_at, content, metadata
  FROM week_messages_raw
  ORDER BY
    COALESCE(metadata->>'message_id', id::text),
    COALESCE((metadata->'loc'->'lines'->>'from')::int, 0) ASC,
    created_at ASC
),
thread_names(thread_id, thread_name) AS (
  VALUES
    (SCAMMER_THREAD_ID, 'Scammer'), (CROWDGEN_THREAD_ID, 'Crowdgen'), (MERCOR_THREAD_ID, 'Mercor'),
    (JOB_OPENING_THREAD_ID, 'Job Opening'), (ONGOING_PROJECT_THREAD_ID, 'Ongoing Project'), (TELUS_THREAD_ID, 'Telus'),
    (INCOGNITO_THREAD_ID, 'Incognito'), (RWS_THREAD_ID, 'RWS'), (WELO_THREAD_ID, 'Welo'),
    (ONEFORMA_THREAD_ID, 'OneForma'), (VERIFIED_PAYOUT_THREAD_ID, 'Verified Payout'), (IMERIT_THREAD_ID, 'iMerit'),
    (PROLIFIC_THREAD_ID, 'Prolific'), (PAIR_RECORDING_THREAD_ID, 'Pair Recording Indo'), (INVISIBLE_THREAD_ID, 'Invisible'),
    (CODING_CLASS_THREAD_ID, 'Coding Class'), (ENGLISH_CLASS_THREAD_ID, 'English Class'), (DATAANNOTATION_THREAD_ID, 'DataAnnotation'),
    (TMAXXX_THREAD_ID, 'TMaxxx'), (OUTLIER_THREAD_ID, 'Outlier'), (TIPS_TRICKS_THREAD_ID, 'Tips & Tricks'), (BABEL_AUDIO_THREAD_ID, 'Babel Audio')
),
thread_counts AS (
  SELECT metadata->>'thread_id' AS thread_id, COUNT(*) AS message_count
  FROM week_messages
  WHERE metadata->>'thread_id' IS NOT NULL AND metadata->>'thread_id' <> ''
  GROUP BY metadata->>'thread_id'
),
top_threads AS (
  SELECT tc.thread_id,
         COALESCE(tn.thread_name, tc.thread_id) AS thread_name,
         tc.message_count
  FROM thread_counts tc
  LEFT JOIN thread_names tn ON tn.thread_id = tc.thread_id::bigint
  ORDER BY tc.message_count DESC
  LIMIT 5
),
top_members AS (
  SELECT split_part(COALESCE(metadata->>'sender_name', metadata->>'username'), ' ', 1) AS first_name,
         COUNT(*) AS message_count
  FROM week_messages
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY message_count DESC
  LIMIT 5
)
SELECT
  (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(wm.metadata->>'sender_name', wm.metadata->>'username'))
    FROM week_messages wm
  ) AS active_members,
  (SELECT json_agg(row_to_json(week_messages)) FROM week_messages) AS messages,
  (SELECT json_agg(row_to_json(top_threads))   FROM top_threads)   AS top_threads,
  (SELECT json_agg(row_to_json(top_members))   FROM top_members)   AS top_members;
